production.note: US model years. First: Edmunds lists the 2017 DB11 '2dr Coupe (5.2L 12cyl Turbo 8A)' at '600 hp @ 6,500 rpm'; Aston's launch release (am-db11-release-2016, 1 March 2016) gives a US price of '$211,995' and says 'first deliveries of the DB11 car are scheduled to begin during the fourth quarter of 2016'. Last: Edmunds' 2018 page (edmunds-db11-2018) still lists 'a turbocharged 5.2-liter V12 engine (600 hp, 516 lb-ft)'; for 2019 (edmunds-db11-2019) the V12 is '630 hp', i.e. the separate DB11 AMR, which replaced this variant. No Aston page states the US model years.

body.note: 2+2 coupe. The DB11 Volante is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

transmission.note: 'Rear mid-mounted ZF eight-speed automatic gearbox with electronic shift-by-wire control system'. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Aston Martin launch release): "Maximum power: 447kW (600bhp / 608PS) at 6500 rpm". 608 PS x 0.98632 = 599.7 hp, rounded to 600. Edmunds gives the US 2017 car '600 hp @ 6,500 rpm' (edmunds-db11-2017); Evo's panel (evo-db11-buying) gives '600bhp @ 6500rpm'. The 2019-on V12 car is the separate DB11 AMR (630 bhp).

weightLb.note: Step 2 of the weight order (major magazine specification panel; Aston publishes only a dry weight). Quote (Evo specs table, 'Aston Martin DB11' column): "Weight | 1870kg". 1,870 kg x 2.20462 = 4,122.6 lb, rounded to 4,123. Evo's panel does not say kerb or dry; it is read as a kerb figure because it is exactly 100 kg above Aston's quoted dry weight ('1770 kg dry weight', am-db11-release-2016) and Evo labels dry figures '(dry)' elsewhere. Standard (only) transmission: 8-speed automatic.

discrepancies.reason: Kerb vs dry. Aston's release gives '1770 kg dry weight' (3,902 lb). Edmunds lists 'Curb Weight: 3,902 lbs.', which is Aston's dry figure converted, not a curb weight. Evo's panel gives 1,870 kg, 100 kg above the dry figure.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Evo's panel figure as the standard car's kerb weight (step 2), which ranks above a dry weight (step 4).
